questions.q_en:
Read the following information and answer the question which follows. "Similar to expert puzzle solvers, Solver S employs systematic problem-solving approaches, ensuring efficient and accurate resolutions to complex challenges." Which of the following can be inferred from the given statement? (An inference is something which is not directly stated but can be derived from the given facts/information in the statement)

1) The efficiency and accuracy of Solver S in resolving complex challenges may be attributed to their systematic problem-solving methods.

2) Solver S utilizes systematic problem-solving approaches, similar to expert puzzle solvers.
questions.solution_en:
The statement mentions that Solver S uses systematic methods, just like expert puzzle solvers, to solve complex problems efficiently and accurately. From this, we can infer (II) directly - Solver S uses systematic approaches. Additionally, since these approaches lead to efficiency and accuracy, it's reasonable to infer (I) - that these qualities may be due to the methods used. Thus, both (I) and (II) logically follow.

Thus, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Two statements numbered I and II are given below. You have to decide whether the data provided in the statements are sufficient to answer the question.

Four persons are sitting in a linear row facing south. Four other persons are sitting in another linear row facing north. The two rows are parallel to each other and each person of one row is facing a person from the other row. Who is sitting to the immediate left of H?

I. B is sitting to the left of G. D is sitting to the immediate left of C. J is facing D. C is sitting at a corner. A is sitting second to the right of K.

II. J is sitting to the immediate left of K. D is sitting second to the right of B. A is facing G. G is sitting second to the left of C.
options_en: If the data in both statements I and II together are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question while the data in statement I alone are not sufficient to answer the question
If the data either in statement I alone or in statement II alone are sufficient to answer the question
If the data in statement I alone are sufficient to answer the question while the data in statement II alone are not sufficient to answer the question
questions.solution_en:
From I alone:

D is sitting to the immediate left of C. J is facing D. C is sitting at a corner.

B is sitting to the left of G. A is sitting second to the right of K.

The eighth person must be H.

In either case, A is sitting to the immediate left of H. Statement I alone is sufficient.

From II alone:

A is facing G. G is sitting second to the left of C. Let us assume that A is facing north.

J is sitting to the immediate left of K. D is sitting second to the right of B.

It cannot be determined who is sitting to the immediate left of H. Statement II alone is not sufficient.

questions.q_en: In a class 220 students appeared in an examination. The rank of Rahul in the list of passed students is 145th from top and 51st from bottom. How many students failed in an examination?
questions.solution_en:
There are total 220 students appeared for the examination.

Rahul ranks 145th from the top and 51st from the bottom in a list of passed students.

So, total number of students in a list = 145 + 51 - 1 = 195 students.

Therefore, number of failed students = 220 - 195 = 25 students.

Thus, 25 students failed in the examination.

questions.q_en:
Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements:

Statements:

Some Nikon is Canon

All Canon are Sony

Some Canon is Philips

Conclusions:

I: Some Nikon is Sony

II: Some Nikon can be Philips

III: No Philips is Sony
questions.solution_en:
Statements:

Some Nikon is Canon

All Canon are Sony

Some Canon is Philips

Some Nikon is Sony: Some Nikon is Canon. All Canon are Sony. Thus, Some Nikon is Sony. So, conclusion I is true.

Some Nikon can be Philips: As there is no direct relation between Nikon and Philips. Thus, Some Nikon can be Philips. So, conclusion II is true.

No Philips is Sony: All Canon are Sony. Some Canon is Philips. Thus, Some Philips is Sony. So, conclusion III is false.

Hence, only conclusions I and II follow.
